entities.summary: Karl Edward Wagner was an American writer, poet, editor, and publisher of horror, science fiction, and heroic fantasy, who was born in Knoxville, Tennessee and originally trained as a psychiatrist. He wrote numerous dark fantasy and horror stories. As an editor, he created a three-volume set of Robert E. Howard's Conan the Barbarian fiction restored to its original form as written, and edited the long-running and genre-defining The Year's Best Horror Stories series for DAW Books. His Carcosa publishing company issued four volumes of the best stories by some of the major authors of the so-called Golden Age pulp magazines.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Wagner's work as an editor and publisher helped preserve and popularize classic horror and fantasy stories, contributing to the development of the genre. His restoration of Robert E. Howard's Conan fiction, in particular, has had a lasting impact on the world of fantasy literature.
